title: When the Wolf Burns Revisited
premise: August Eriksen, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things, discovers tonight's date in the Vellum of Thirteenth Moons—a prophecy written a century ago foretelling that the storm-caller will either break the moon-seal or die trying. As the guild's clients begin hunting August, they learn the prophecy was authored by their own vanished mentor, who sealed the ancient war away at the cost of August's exile. Torn between the guild family that shielded them and the truth that the seal is fed by stolen storm-blood, August must choose: preserve the lie that keeps the peace, or unleash the storm and be judged outside any law. In the end, August breaks the seal on the thirteenth turn, takes the war's blame onto themselves, and walks into exile again—alive, unmasked, and finally free.
about_author: Casper Zhou is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing salvaged ship ledgers before turning to fantasy. They write stories about people who keep records of things the world would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Years
chapters.summary: August Eriksen, POV. In the guild's fog-bound counting house, August balances ledgers of traded impossibilities while suppressing every flicker of their storm-calling. A routine audit turns strange when a client pays in a page torn from a century-old prophecy. The beat is wary comfort cracking at the edges: invisibility has been a discipline, and it is beginning to fail.

chapters.title: Tonight, Written in Old Ink
chapters.summary: August, POV. Deciphering the page, August finds tonight's exact date in the Vellum of Thirteenth Moons, naming the storm-caller by a childhood title no one living should know. They conceal it from guildmaster Ysolde. The beat is dread sharpening into resolve: the past has found a way to schedule itself.

chapters.title: Clients Who Smell Rain
chapters.summary: Ysolde, POV. The guild's strangest patrons arrive in one night—ash-priests, a moon-tithed noble, a mute cartographer—all asking, too casually, after a storm-caller. Ysolde realizes someone sold the guild's silence. The beat is protective suspicion: she has kept August's secret for years and will not surrender it cheaply.

chapters.title: What the Seal Is Fed
chapters.summary: August, POV. Following the cartographer's stolen map, August finds the moon-seal beneath the drowned chapel and discovers it drinks storm-blood—harvested, for a century, from exiles like them. The beat is horrified recognition: the peace they resented was built on a slaughter they narrowly escaped.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Last Ledger
chapters.summary: August, POV. In the mentor's hidden vault, August finds the original Vellum and a confession: the mentor wrote the prophecy to force a successor's hand, then engineered August's exile to hide them from the harvesters. The beat is grief braided with betrayal—love and manipulation in the same hand.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Priced Per Page
chapters.summary: Ysolde, POV. The ash-priests offer Ysolde the guild's survival in exchange for August. She stalls, burns the offer, and quietly arms the guild's oddities for war. The beat is fierce, unsentimental loyalty: family is a debt she intends to pay in full.

chapters.title: Thirteenth Turn Rising
chapters.summary: August, POV. The moon nears its impossible thirteenth turn; the seal frays and the first ancient things wake in the fens. August must choose between re-feeding the seal with their own blood—dying as the prophecy's martyr—or breaking it and risking war. The beat is cornered clarity: there is no innocent option left.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Vellum
chapters.summary: August, POV. Climax. At the drowned chapel, August shatters the seal and calls a storm a century in the making, fighting the risen ancients alongside Ysolde and the guild's impossible inventory. August refuses the prophecy's binary—martyr or tyrant—and writes a third ending in lightning. The beat is cathartic, terrifying power finally claimed.

chapters.title: Judgment Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Ysolde, POV. The kingdoms convene a tribunal with no jurisdiction over guild ground, demanding August's head for breaking the seal. Ysolde produces the mentor's confession and the harvest ledgers, turning justice back on the courts. The beat is vindication with a cost: truth wins, but not cleanly.

chapters.title: Exile, Twice Kept
chapters.summary: August, POV. Acquitted by no one and pardoned by no one, August chooses exile again—this time freely, ledger closed, name known. Ysolde gives them a blank book for whatever comes next. The final beat is bittersweet freedom: August leaves not as a hidden thing, but as a person the storm no longer owns.
